$comment: Reason ids the library can report, strongest first: a verdict lists its reasons in this order. Ids are a public contract: added, never renamed within a major version. half: where the evidence is read. names: whether the reason can name an agent (signer, token, page-declaration, a product name) or never does (null). Each reason also records its known collisions (collision_kind: none-known, untested or agent-surface, where a person inside an agent's own surface is reported as that agent by design) and when it was last tested.

reasons.summary: A Web Bot Auth signature on the request verified against a key bundled with this release.
reasons.collisions: No person's browser signs requests. It authenticates the signer's infrastructure, not who controls the session: a person who takes over a hosted browser session is still reported as the signer.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: The hosting platform verified the request as a known bot (Cloudflare's verified-bot category).
reasons.collisions: No person's browser is a verified bot. It says some verified bot sent the request, which includes search crawlers, not which agent.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: The request carries a Web Bot Auth signature that did not verify here: an unknown or expired key, a signature outside its window, or a check that failed.
reasons.collisions: No person's browser sends a Web Bot Auth signature. Anyone can send the headers, so it is a declaration, never authentication.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: The user agent contains a token that declares software: an agent, fetcher, crawler, link previewer or HTTP client.
reasons.collisions: No person's browser sends these tokens. Anyone can, so it is a declaration, never authentication.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: The page's own navigator declares a hosted browser engine.
reasons.collisions: No person's browser declares these engines. Forgeable like any declaration.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: navigator.webdriver is true: the browser declares that automation controls it.
reasons.collisions: None in 44 human documents (a Windows VM, a Linux container, Safari, Firefox, an iPhone, DevTools open). It says the browser is automated, not who drives it; a person using a browser that automation launched would match (untested).
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: The user agent declares headless Chrome.
reasons.collisions: No person browses headless; a person driving a remote headless session would match (untested).
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: 1Password's accessor family on the credential methods, in Chrome 139 or later on Linux x86_64 rendering WebGL with SwiftShader: Muse's cloud browser.
reasons.collisions: 1Password alone installs the accessor family for every user (measured with 1Password 8.12, 3 October); the rule also needs Muse's host. A person matches only with 1Password, Linux, and Chrome launched with --enable-unsafe-swiftshader (untested; rare). Another automation host running 1Password would be named muse.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-03: Muse 21 of 21 evaluable documents (28 September, 1 October); 0 of 82 human documents, 0 of 4 with 1Password

reasons.summary: The credential methods are wrapped the way Instinct's cloud desktop wraps them; counts only together with the GeeTest pair.
reasons.collisions: A credential or CAPTCHA extension that wraps only get and create with anonymous one-argument functions (none known); a person on the same remote browser. Counts only with instinct.geetest.accessor-pair.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: The GeeTest initialisers are the accessor pair Instinct installs; counts only together with the credential wrappers.
reasons.collisions: Pages that load GeeTest define plain functions, not accessors; a CAPTCHA-solver extension a person uses might install accessors (untested). Counts only with instinct.credentials.wrappers.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: window.prompt has the Codex in-app browser's shape; counts only with a second Codex shell signal.
reasons.collisions: A person browsing the Codex in-app browser by hand (measured: 4 of 4 documents). It identifies the browser, not who acts in it.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: The keyboard layout map is empty, as in the Codex in-app browser; counts only with a second Codex shell signal.
reasons.collisions: A person in the Codex in-app browser (measured). It identifies the browser, not who acts in it.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: The Codex in-app browser's overlay is attached to the document; counts only with a second Codex shell signal.
reasons.collisions: A person in the Codex in-app browser: the browser draws it for everyone. Other overlays at the maximum z-index (screen recorders, translation and writing extensions) are a J1 control.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: ChatGPT for Chrome's activity badge was drawn on the page while its agent acted.
reasons.collisions: A person taking the tab over in the seconds before the badge is removed; it left within seconds of the agent's turn in both takeover runs.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: Claude for Chrome's activity marker was drawn on the page while its agent acted.
reasons.collisions: A person taking the tab over before the glow is removed; it left at the end of the agent's turn (17 s, 20 s), before the person's first click, in both takeover runs.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: Trusted input arrived while the document was hidden yet reported focus, which needs focus emulation.
reasons.collisions: No known way for a person to deliver input to a hidden document; focus while hidden needs focus emulation. None in 44 human documents.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents

reasons.summary: A trusted pointerdown arrived while the document was hidden, which no person can produce.
reasons.collisions: No known way for a person to click in a hidden document. None in 44 human documents.
reasons.tested: 2026-10-02: replayed on every benchmark sheet (rule set 1.6.0), with 57 human control documents
